common_name: Longissima Alba Wisteria (Long-Raceme White Japanese Wisteria)

planting.note: Plant container vines in late winter or spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Longissima Alba requires a very sturdy trellis, pergola, or arbor that can support the mature vine weight.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade on a sturdy support structure able to bear significant long-term weight. Longissima Alba is a Japanese wisteria cultivar bred for exceptionally long, pure white flower racemes that can extend well over a foot, opening in sequence from the base of the cluster toward the tip for a prolonged, cascading bloom display in late spring, carrying the classic sweet wisteria fragrance. Like other Japanese wisteria it twines clockwise around its support and grows into an enormously heavy, long-lived woody vine over years, so choose a permanent, oversized structure rather than a typical garden trellis. Prune twice yearly, in summer after bloom and again in late winter, to control size and encourage the short flowering spurs that produce the best bloom.

common_name: Incense Passionflower (Fragrant Deep Purple Hybrid Passionflower)

planting.note: Plant container vines after last frost in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Incense is hardier than many tropical passionflower hybrids and can die back to the roots in a hard freeze before resprouting in spring.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun and provide a trellis or fence for the vigorous tendrils. Incense is a hybrid passionflower bred from the cold-hardy native Passiflora incarnata and prized for its large, intensely fragrant, deep purple flowers with a dramatic fringed filament corona, combining showy color with a noticeably stronger scent than many other ornamental passionflower hybrids. It is considerably more cold-hardy than tropical passionflower species thanks to its native parentage, often surviving winters as a root-hardy perennial that dies back and resprouts from the ground each spring outside its evergreen range. Deadhead spent flowers to encourage continued bloom through summer, and provide a sturdy support for the fast-growing, twining vine.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun on a strong, permanent support such as a large arbor or sturdy fence; like the species, Flava spreads by root suckers and can be aggressive, so site it where spread is welcome or manageable.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun against a strong, permanent structure, since this vigorous woody vine becomes heavy with age. Flava is a yellow-flowered selection of the native trumpet creeper, bearing the same large, trumpet-shaped summer blooms and aerial-rootlet climbing habit as the wild orange-red species but in a bright, clear golden-yellow that draws hummingbirds just as reliably. Like the straight species it is an extremely vigorous, self-clinging vine that spreads by root suckers and can become weedy or damage structures like siding and gutters if not sited and pruned with care, so give it a dedicated, sturdy support well away from the house. Prune hard in late winter to control size, since flowers form on new growth and heavy pruning does not sacrifice the coming season's bloom.
